fullSentence: When it comes to geography, there is very little that Luis doesn’t know.
gapFill: There are very __________________ when it comes to geography.
explanation: Use few with plural countable nouns. The phrase gaps in someone’s knowledge refers to things that person does not know.

fullSentence: Daniel was going to take his sister to the concert, but it looks as if he’s forgotten.
gapFill: Daniel __________________ taking his sister to the concert.
answer: must have forgotten that he was
explanation: Use must have + past participle to make a strong deduction about the past: he must have forgotten.

fullSentence: The fence was removed and, as a result, the neighbours no longer feel they have privacy.
gapFill: Removing the fence has __________________ for the neighbours.
answer: resulted in a loss of privacy
resulted in the loss of privacy
led to a loss of privacy
led to the loss of privacy
explanation: Result in and lead to are followed by a noun or noun phrase: resulted in / led to a loss of privacy.

fullSentence: Sasha definitely didn’t plan to return to the flat until the heating was fixed.
gapFill: Sasha had absolutely no __________________ to the flat until the heating was fixed.
answer: intention at all of going back
tags: C1, verb patterns, fixed phrase, formal
explanation: The pattern is have no intention of + -ing: she had no intention of returning.

fullSentence: Irene was going to join us this evening, but it seems she’s decided not to.
gapFill: Irene seems __________________ joining us this evening.
answer: to have changed her mind about
tags: C1, perfect, verb patterns, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: After seem, use the perfect infinitive to have + past participle to refer to an earlier action or change: she seems to have changed her mind.

fullSentence: Alessio thought the driving test would be easy to pass.
gapFill: Alessio was under the __________________ be easy to pass the driving test.
explanation: Be under the impression (that) + clause means to believe something, often when that belief may be mistaken.

fullSentence: Dr Lee’s negotiating skills quickly impressed her colleagues.
gapFill: Among her colleagues, Dr Lee soon gained __________________ a skilled negotiator.
tags: C1, noun phrases, fixed phrase, prepositions
explanation: Use gain a reputation for + -ing to describe how someone comes to be regarded by other people: gain a reputation for being a skilled negotiator.

fullSentence: If you hadn’t helped me, I would never have got the sofa through the door.
gapFill: But __________________, I would never have got the sofa through the door.
answer: for the help you gave me
for the help that you gave me
for the help which you gave me
explanation: But for + noun means if it had not been for: But for your help = If you hadn’t helped me.

fullSentence: Most fans think Brazil will win the final against France.
gapFill: Most fans think France __________________ the final.
answer: will be beaten by Brazil in
will get beaten by Brazil in
explanation: The future passive is formed with will be + past participle: France will be beaten by Brazil.

fullSentence: The alarm system is there so that no valuables can be stolen during the night.
gapFill: The alarm system is designed to __________________ stolen during the night.
tags: C1, passive voice, verb patterns, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Use prevent + object + (from) + -ing. In a passive structure, this becomes prevent valuables from being stolen.

fullSentence: The hacker used special software so as not to leave any trace of the attack.
gapFill: The hacker used software in __________________ any trace of the attack.
tags: C1, verb patterns, purpose, linking, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Avoid is followed by a gerund: avoid leaving. Expressions such as in order to, in an attempt to and in an effort to can introduce purpose.

fullSentence: Even if your phone is beyond repair, you’ll still be charged for the service.
gapFill: Whether your phone __________________ not, you’ll still be charged for the repair service.
tags: C1, passive voice, modal verbs, possibility
explanation: Whether ... or not presents two alternatives. With a modal passive, use can + be + past participle: can be repaired.

fullSentence: I had no success in contacting Javier before the deadline.
gapFill: I __________________ hold of Javier before the deadline.
tags: C1, verb patterns, modal verbs, ability
explanation: Manage is followed by the to-infinitive: manage to get. In the negative, didn’t manage to means that the attempt was unsuccessful.

fullSentence: Because of the metro strike, all of the guests arrived late to the event.
gapFill: Because of the metro strike, not __________________ to the event on time.
answer: even one of the guests turned up
one of the guests turned up
explanation: Not even one and not a single + singular noun strongly emphasise that the number was zero.

fullSentence: It was a mistake to make Lena responsible for leading the tour group on her first day.
gapFill: Lena should __________________ of leading the tour group on her first day.
answer: not have been put in charge
never have been put in charge
not have been left in charge
never have been left in charge
not have been placed in charge
never have been placed in charge
tags: C1, passive voice, past modals, modals
explanation: Use should not have + past participle to criticise a past decision or action. Put someone in charge of + -ing means make them responsible for something.

fullSentence: Someone has suggested changing the school’s uniform policy.
gapFill: A suggestion has __________________ the school’s uniform policy.
explanation: Put forward is a phrasal verb meaning propose or suggest. In the passive: a suggestion has been put forward.

fullSentence: The guide says it will take us less than a week to cross the mountains.
gapFill: The guide says that we __________________ in less than a week.
explanation: Use the future perfect will have + past participle for something that will be completed before a future point: we will have crossed the mountains.

fullSentence: By the end of the discussion, the team had agreed on the proposed changes.
gapFill: By the end of the discussion, an __________________ the proposed changes.
tags: C1, passive voice, noun phrases, formal
explanation: Reach an agreement on/about something means agree formally. The noun phrase can be made passive: an agreement had been reached.

fullSentence: Maya succeeded in passing the exam, even though she had a cold.
gapFill: Despite __________________ pass the exam.
answer: having a cold, Maya managed to
explanation: Despite is followed by a noun, pronoun or gerund rather than a finite clause: despite having a cold. Manage to + infinitive expresses successful achievement.

fullSentence: Hardly any of my students know who James Baldwin is.
gapFill: Among my students, very __________________ the author James Baldwin.
answer: few of them have heard of
few of them have heard about
explanation: Very few + plural noun means almost none. Have heard of someone means know that the person exists or know something about them.

fullSentence: Emma would do anything at all to help her family.
gapFill: There is absolutely __________________ to help her family.
answer: nothing that Emma would not do
nothing which Emma would not do
explanation: Nothing ... would not do expresses the idea of being willing to do absolutely anything: there is nothing she would not do.

fullSentence: I don’t think we’ll see Max before he flies to Tokyo.
gapFill: There’s __________________ Max before he flies to Tokyo.
answer: little likelihood that we will see
explanation: Little likelihood expresses low probability. It can be followed by of + -ing or by a clause: little likelihood of seeing him / little likelihood that we will see him.

fullSentence: Although Peter travels frequently, he’s always losing his suitcase.
gapFill: Although Peter travels frequently, this __________________ he’s lost his suitcase.
answer: will not be the first time
will not be the first occasion
explanation: Use this is not the first time + present perfect to talk about something that has happened before: this is not the first time he’s lost it.

fullSentence: When I finally got to the platform, the train was about to leave.
gapFill: The train was on the point __________________ I arrived at the platform.
answer: of leaving by the time that
explanation: On the point of + -ing means about to do something. By the time introduces the later event used as the time reference.

fullSentence: Olivia couldn’t possibly afford any of the meals in that restaurant.
gapFill: The meals in that restaurant are __________________ pay for.
answer: far too expensive for Olivia to
explanation: Far can intensify too + adjective: far too expensive. The pattern for + person + to-infinitive shows who is unable to do the action.

fullSentence: Could Sofia have left her umbrella at home this morning?
gapFill: I __________________ her umbrella at home this morning.
answer: wonder if Sofia could have left
wonder whether Sofia could have left
tags: C1, modal verbs, past modals, indirect questions, questions
explanation: After wonder, use if or whether to introduce an indirect question, with normal statement word order: I wonder whether Sofia has left it at home.

fullSentence: The accident last year led to the imposition of tougher safety rules.
gapFill: Tougher rules __________________ result of last year's accident.
explanation: As a result of + noun expresses cause. The verb impose can also be used in the passive: tougher rules were imposed as a result of the accident.

fullSentence: We could do our chores first and then go to the football match.
gapFill: Why don’t __________________ to the football match?
answer: we do our chores before going
we finish our chores before going
we do our chores before we go
we finish our chores before we go
we complete our chores before going
we complete our chores before we go
explanation: Before can be followed either by a gerund or by a full clause: before going / before we go.

fullSentence: I was really shocked when my cousin told me what had happened the day before.
gapFill: I was shocked by my __________________ what had happened the day before.
tags: C1, noun phrases, formal, fixed phrase
explanation: An account of something is a description or report of it. Use the possessive before account: my cousin’s account of what happened.

fullSentence: A woman led a major space mission several decades ago.
gapFill: It __________________ a woman first led a major space mission.
explanation: Use it is / has been + period of time + since + past simple to say how long ago something happened.

fullSentence: People often say that Jenny looks and behaves just like her aunt.
gapFill: People often comment on the extent to __________________ her aunt.
explanation: The formal structure the extent to which means how much or how strongly something is true. Take after means resemble an older family member.

fullSentence: By the end of the workshop, the group had agreed on the next steps.
gapFill: By the end of the workshop, an __________________ how to proceed.
tags: C1, passive voice, noun phrases, formal
explanation: Reach an agreement can be expressed in the passive as an agreement was/had been reached. Use on or about before the subject of the agreement.

fullSentence: By the end of the week, it will be two years since Samantha came to Paris.
gapFill: By the end of the week, Samantha _____________________ two years.
answer: will have been in Paris for
will have lived in Paris for
will have been living in Paris for
explanation: Use the future perfect with for + period to show how long something will have continued by a future point: will have been in Paris for two years.

fullSentence: A number of open-air shows had to be cancelled owing to the stormy weather.
gapFill: Stormy weather _____________________ of a number of open-air shows.
explanation: Lead to expresses a result and is followed by a noun or gerund: led to the cancellation / cancelling of the shows.

fullSentence: During the meeting, the director did not mention the training programme.
gapFill: During the meeting, the director _____________________ the training programme.
answer: did not make any reference to
explanation: Make reference to is a formal equivalent of mention. Negative forms include made no reference to and did not make any reference to.

fullSentence: "I'm not staying late again," said Daniel.
gapFill: Daniel made _____________________ willing to stay late at the office.
answer: it clear that he was not
explanation: The fixed structure is make it clear (that) + clause: Daniel made it clear that he was not willing to stay.

fullSentence: Jordan was just about to leave the flat when the doorbell rang.
gapFill: Jordan _____________________ the flat when the doorbell rang.
answer: was on the point of leaving
explanation: Be on the point of + -ing means be just about to do something: was on the point of leaving.

fullSentence: Ivy was thrilled to be selected for the scholarship.
gapFill: Much to _____________________ selected for the scholarship.
explanation: Much to + possessive + emotion noun introduces someone’s strong reaction: Much to her delight, ...

fullSentence: The ticket discount led to a rise in attendance at the event.
gapFill: Attendance at the event _____________________ the ticket discount.
answer: went up as a result of
explanation: As a result of + noun introduces the cause of a result: attendance rose as a result of the discount.

fullSentence: Maya would have emailed back if she had had more time.
gapFill: Maya didn’t email back _____________________ time.
explanation: Be short of + noun means not have enough of something: she was short of time.

fullSentence: Elliot promised to call as soon as he arrived at the station.
gapFill: Elliot said that _____________________ he arrived at the station.
answer: he would call the moment that
he was going to call the moment that
he was going to call the moment
explanation: The moment (that) + clause means as soon as. In reported speech, will normally changes to would: he said he would call the moment he arrived.

fullSentence: Leo doesn't plan to travel abroad this summer.
gapFill: Leo has _____________________ abroad this summer.
explanation: Use have no intention of + -ing to say that someone does not plan to do something: no intention of travelling abroad.

fullSentence: Hopefully, the economy will improve soon.
gapFill: Hopefully, there’ll be _____________________ better in the economy soon.
explanation: A change for the better is a fixed expression meaning an improvement.

fullSentence: 'Do you fancy seeing the new film at the cinema?' Liam asked his cousin.
gapFill: Liam asked his cousin whether _____________________ the new film at the cinema.
answer: he would be interested in seeing
she would be interested in seeing
tags: C1, gerunds and infinitives, reported speech
explanation: Interested is followed by in + -ing: interested in seeing the film. In a reported yes/no question, use whether or if followed by statement word order.

fullSentence: Luis hasn't messaged me in ages.
answer: have not heard from Luis for
have not heard from Luis in
have heard nothing from Luis for
have heard nothing from Luis in
have not heard anything from Luis for
have not heard anything from Luis in
explanation: Use the present perfect with for/in ages to describe a situation continuing up to the present: I haven’t heard from Luis for ages.

fullSentence: The team is almost certain to win the tournament.
gapFill: The team has _____________________ the tournament.
explanation: Have every chance of + -ing means be very likely to do something: the team has every chance of winning.

fullSentence: The cost of vegetables has gone up significantly recently.
gapFill: There _____________________ the cost of vegetables recently.
answer: has been a sharp rise in
has been a significant rise in
explanation: Trends can be expressed with a noun phrase after there has been: there has been a significant rise in the cost.

fullSentence: If she fails the course, who knows what will happen next!
gapFill: If she fails the course, _____________________ what will happen next!
explanation: There is no knowing is a fixed expression meaning it is impossible to know or predict something.

fullSentence: We've all been impressed by Amira’s attitude to challenges.
gapFill: Amira’s attitude to challenges has _____________________ us.
answer: made a great impression on all of
made a big impression on all of
made an impression on all of
explanation: The collocation is make an impression on someone: her attitude made a great impression on us.

fullSentence: Jay’s startup didn’t achieve much success during its first year.
gapFill: Jay’s startup _____________________ during its first year.
tags: C1, comparatives and superlatives, intensifiers, so/such
explanation: Successful is the adjective formed from the noun success. After be, use the adjective: the startup was not so successful.

fullSentence: It was probably a bad idea to lend your laptop to Ben.
gapFill: I don’t think _____________________ your laptop to Ben.
explanation: Use I don’t think + should have + past participle to say that a past action was probably a mistake: I don’t think you should have lent your laptop.

fullSentence: The teacher thought it was strange that Mark hadn't replied to the email.
gapFill: The teacher found _____________________ the email quite unusual.
explanation: Failure to + infinitive is a formal noun structure meaning that someone did not do something: Mark's failure to reply.

fullSentence: I doubt you'll have much trouble following the instructions.
gapFill: I doubt _____________________ to follow the instructions.
explanation: The pattern find it + adjective + to-infinitive means experience something as difficult, easy, strange, etc.: find it difficult to follow.

fullSentence: Experts think Leila has the ability to win the national title in tennis.
gapFill: Experts think Leila _____________________ the national title in tennis.
explanation: Capable is followed by of + -ing: she is capable of winning. It expresses ability or potential.

fullSentence: Gina was asked to give an explanation for making the error.
gapFill: Gina was asked to _____________________ the error.
explanation: Explain can be followed by why + clause: explain why she made the error. A past perfect form can be used when the action happened earlier.

fullSentence: They put Omar in charge of organising the school event.
gapFill: Omar _____________________ organising the school event.
explanation: Make someone responsible for + -ing can be used in the passive: Omar was made responsible for organising the event.

fullSentence: Do you think Arjun is likely to win the election?
gapFill: Do you think Arjun is in _____________________ the election?
explanation: Be in with a chance of + -ing means have a realistic possibility of succeeding: in with a chance of winning.

fullSentence: Theo says that only his cousin knows about the surprise party.
gapFill: Theo claims that _____________________ knows about the surprise party.
answer: apart from his cousin no one
no one apart from his cousin
explanation: Apart from means except for. It can come before or after the person or thing being excluded: apart from his cousin, nobody knew.

fullSentence: Rita really should get her glasses repaired.
gapFill: It's _____________________ her glasses repaired.
explanation: It's high time + past simple is used to say that something should already have happened: It's high time Rita got her glasses repaired.

fullSentence: Despite all their efforts, the door wouldn’t open.
gapFill: No matter _____________________, the door wouldn’t open.
explanation: No matter how + adjective/adverb expresses concession: no matter how hard they tried = despite all their efforts.

fullSentence: When it comes to science fiction, Daria knows everything.
gapFill: As _____________________, Daria knows everything.
answer: far as science fiction is concerned
explanation: As far as ... is concerned is a fixed expression meaning when considering or talking about a particular subject.

fullSentence: Nina never thought of asking me for help.
answer: never occurred to Nina to ask
had never occurred to Nina to ask
explanation: The pattern it occurs to someone to + infinitive means that an idea enters their mind: it never occurred to Nina to ask.

fullSentence: Cavalli painted exotic scenes of the jungle although he had never set foot outside Europe.
gapFill: Cavalli painted exotic scenes of the jungle _______________________ set foot outside Europe.
explanation: In spite of is followed by a noun or gerund. To refer to an earlier action, use having + past participle: in spite of never having set foot outside Europe.

fullSentence: Zara didn’t fully grasp the situation until she listened to Luis’s voicemail.
gapFill: It _______________________ she listened to Luis’s voicemail that Zara fully grasped the situation.
explanation: The cleft structure it was only when/after/once ... that emphasises the point at which something finally happened.

fullSentence: Due to its high cost, the new gadget might never gain widespread popularity.
gapFill: The cost of the new gadget may _______________________ widely popular.
tags: C1, formal, verb patterns, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Use prevent + object + (from) + -ing: prevent it from becoming popular. From can often be omitted.

fullSentence: The island is abundant in terms of biodiversity and untouched ecosystems.
gapFill: The island has a lot _______________________ terms of biodiversity and untouched ecosystems.
explanation: Have a lot to offer means have many positive qualities or advantages. In terms of introduces the particular area being considered.

fullSentence: Simone says she prefers to cook dinner by herself.
gapFill: Simone says that _______________________ cook dinner with anyone else.
tags: C1, modal verbs, formal, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Would rather is followed by the bare infinitive. To express a negative preference, use would rather not + verb: she'd rather not cook with anyone else.

fullSentence: To succeed as a nurse, you need to have an enormous amount of patience.
gapFill: Being a nurse calls _______________________.
answer: for a great deal of patience
for a good deal of patience
tags: C1, phrasal verbs, noun phrases, quantifiers, formal
explanation: Call for means require or need. A great/good deal of is used with uncountable nouns: calls for a great deal of patience.

fullSentence: The suspect insisted that he hadn't gone anywhere near the building that night.
gapFill: The suspect claimed not _______________________ near the building that night.
tags: C1, verb patterns, gerunds and infinitives, perfect
explanation: After verbs such as claim, use the perfect infinitive to have + past participle to refer to an earlier action: claimed not to have gone anywhere near the building.

fullSentence: I need to renew my ID before travelling next month.
gapFill: I need _______________________ before travelling next month.
explanation: Get + object + past participle is a causative structure used when someone arranges for something to be done: get my ID renewed.

fullSentence: I'm going to eat fewer crisps this year.
gapFill: I'm going to _______________________ of crisps I eat this year.
explanation: Cut down on + noun means reduce how much of something you use or consume: cut down on the amount of crisps.

fullSentence: The majority of the issues came about because no one was leading the team.
gapFill: It was the _______________________ most of the issues within the team.
tags: C1, noun phrases, relative clauses, cleft sentences
explanation: The cleft structure it was ... that/which places emphasis on the cause: It was the lack of leadership that caused the problems.

fullSentence: Experts believe that many people cannot keep their finances under control.
gapFill: Many people are thought _______________________ their finances under control.
explanation: Passive reporting structures use be + past participle + infinitive: many people are thought to be unable to keep their finances under control.

fullSentence: Leo insisted that he had never seen the missing notebook.
gapFill: Leo _______________________ the missing notebook.
tags: C1, verb patterns, gerunds and infinitives, reported speech, reporting verbs
explanation: Deny is followed by a gerund. Use having + past participle when the denied action happened earlier: denied having seen the notebook.

fullSentence: This suitcase is incredibly heavy — I'd really appreciate some help getting it to the taxi.
gapFill: This suitcase is really heavy so I'd _______________________ help me carry it to the taxi.
explanation: Be grateful if + subject + could/would is a polite way of making a request: I'd be grateful if you could help me.

fullSentence: The team started testing the new app immediately after the planning phase.
gapFill: The team lost _______________________ testing the new app after the planning phase.
tags: C1, fixed phrase, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Lose no time or lose little time (in) + -ing means begin doing something immediately or almost immediately.

fullSentence: The sculpture is so well preserved that it’s difficult to believe it's over 500 years old.
gapFill: The sculpture is in such good _______________________ believe it’s over 500 years old.
answer: condition that it is hard to
tags: C1, fixed phrase, noun phrases, intensifiers, so/such
explanation: The pattern such + adjective + noun + that introduces a result: in such good condition that it is hard to believe its age.

fullSentence: By the time we got to the bakery, all the bread had gone.
gapFill: By the time we got to the bakery, there _______________________ loaf left.
explanation: Not a single + singular countable noun strongly emphasises that there were none: not a single loaf was left.

fullSentence: The performance was too loud for us to stay until the end.
gapFill: If _______________________ noise, we might have stayed until the end of the performance.
answer: there had not been so much
explanation: In a third conditional, use if + past perfect and might/would have + past participle: If there hadn't been so much noise, we might have stayed.

fullSentence: The number of students registering for evening classes went down last year.
gapFill: There _______________________ number of students registering for evening classes last year.
explanation: Changes in quantities can be expressed with there was + a noun of change + in: there was a fall in the number of students.

fullSentence: If you pay late, your reservation will be cancelled.
gapFill: Failure to _______________________ your reservation being cancelled.
answer: pay on time will result in
explanation: Failure to + infinitive means not doing something. Result in is followed by a noun or gerund: failure to pay will result in your reservation being cancelled.

fullSentence: After her operation, Ella recovered quickly and rejoined the team.
gapFill: After her operation, Ella _______________________ and rejoined the team.
explanation: Make a recovery is a common collocation. Adjectives such as quick, fast and speedy describe how rapidly someone recovers.

fullSentence: Most students didn’t pay attention to what the teacher said.
gapFill: Few students _______________________ what the teacher said.
explanation: Take notice of means pay attention to. After a limiting subject such as few students, any or much is commonly used in the object phrase: few students took any notice.

fullSentence: I hadn’t realised how small the performer was until I saw him live.
gapFill: It was only _______________________ me realise how small the performer was.
explanation: The cleft structure it was only ... that is used to emphasise the thing that caused a realisation: It was only seeing him live that made me realise.

fullSentence: It’s really tough creating new content for the event each year.
gapFill: How difficult _______________________ with new content for the event each year.
answer: it can be to come up
explanation: How + adjective + subject + be can form an exclamative structure: how difficult it is. Come up with means think of or produce an idea.

fullSentence: Claims for pay must be submitted before the deadline.
gapFill: You have _______________________ your pay claims before the deadline.
explanation: Put in is a phrasal verb meaning formally submit something, especially a request, claim or application: put in a pay claim.

fullSentence: There are various ways of avoiding mosquito bites.
gapFill: Mosquito bites can _______________________ various ways.
explanation: The modal passive is formed with modal + be + past participle: mosquito bites can be prevented.

fullSentence: Learning to use a fax machine is a waste of time.
gapFill: I can’t _______________________ how to use a fax machine.
tags: C1, gerunds and infinitives, fixed phrase
explanation: See the point in/of + -ing means understand the purpose or value of doing something: I can't see the point in learning it.

fullSentence: Turn off your phone completely during the performance.
gapFill: Under no _______________________ your phone switched on during the performance.
explanation: After a negative expression such as under no circumstances at the beginning of a sentence, use inversion: Under no circumstances should you leave your phone switched on.

fullSentence: This firm has a great reputation locally.
gapFill: The firm _______________________ of in the local area.
explanation: Be highly thought of and be highly spoken of are passive expressions meaning have a very good reputation.

fullSentence: I’m sure Yara will become a famous architect one day.
gapFill: I think it’s only _______________________ Yara becomes a famous architect.
tags: C1, fixed phrase, future, noun phrases
explanation: It's only a matter of time before ... means that something is considered certain to happen eventually.

fullSentence: This food festival should attract everyone—up to twenty food trucks are expected.
gapFill: This festival will appeal _______________________ as twenty food trucks are expected.
explanation: As many as + number emphasises that a quantity is surprisingly or notably large: as many as twenty food trucks.

fullSentence: At the start of the show, the presenters discussed online privacy.
gapFill: The presenters began the show _______________________ online privacy.
explanation: Begin with + noun describes the first part of something: begin with a discussion. Begin by + -ing describes the first action: begin by having a discussion.

fullSentence: Camila’s parents were certain she’d become a great violinist.
gapFill: Camila’s parents were _______________________ she’d become a great violinist.
tags: C1, formal, fixed phrase, prepositions, noun phrases
explanation: Be in no doubt (that) means be completely certain. The equivalent negative form is not be in any doubt.

fullSentence: My uncle had completely forgotten that he had emailed me.
gapFill: My uncle didn’t _______________________ emailing me.
explanation: Have no/any recollection of + noun or -ing means not remember something: he didn't have any recollection of emailing me.

fullSentence: If Asha hadn’t pursued photography, she might have become a famous chef.
gapFill: If Asha hadn’t pursued photography, she might have _______________________ herself as a chef.
explanation: Make a name for yourself means become well known or successful in a particular field: make a name for herself as a chef.

fullSentence: Staff shouldn’t expect a guaranteed locker.
gapFill: The staff shouldn’t _______________________ allocated a locker.
explanation: Count on + noun/-ing means rely on or confidently expect something: staff should not count on being allocated a locker.

fullSentence: ‘I’ve had enough of people being rude to me,’ said Ava.
gapFill: ‘I’m not prepared _______________________ from people any longer,’ said Ava.
answer: to put up with any rudeness
to put up with rude behaviour
to put up with any rude behaviour
explanation: Put up with is a phrasal verb meaning tolerate something unpleasant: put up with rude behaviour.

fullSentence: This holiday is affordable, provided we don’t eat at expensive places.
gapFill: We _______________________ as we avoid expensive places.
answer: can afford this holiday as long
can afford the holiday as long
can afford this holiday so long
can afford the holiday so long
explanation: As long as and so long as introduce a condition and mean provided that: we can afford the holiday as long as we avoid expensive places.

fullSentence: Since Carlos is out of practice, he probably won’t win the race.
gapFill: Carlos has almost _______________________ the race, since he’s out of practice.
tags: C1, probability, noun phrases, fixed phrase
explanation: Have no chance of + -ing means that something is extremely unlikely or impossible: he has almost no chance of winning.

fullSentence: Nina was just about to leave the café when her cousin arrived.
gapFill: Nina was just _______________________ the café when her cousin arrived.
explanation: Be on the point of + -ing means be just about to do something: Nina was on the point of leaving.

fullSentence: Due to the storm, Theo wasn’t able to leave his apartment.
gapFill: The storm _______________________ Theo to leave his apartment.
explanation: Use make it + adjective + for someone + to-infinitive to describe the effect of a situation: the storm made it impossible for Theo to leave.

fullSentence: Theo’s likely to be dismissed if he keeps arguing with his manager.
gapFill: If he keeps arguing with his manager, Theo’s _______________________ from his job.
explanation: Be in danger of + -ing means be at risk of something happening: he is in danger of being dismissed.

fullSentence: Although the students weren’t listening, the lecturer stayed calm.
gapFill: Although the students weren’t _______________________ saying, the lecturer stayed calm.
answer: paying attention to what he was
paying attention to what she was
paying any attention to what he was
paying any attention to what she was
explanation: The expression is pay attention to + noun or clause: pay attention to what someone is saying. Any can strengthen the negative form: not paying any attention.

fullSentence: Can Andre handle this task with no previous experience?
gapFill: Will Andre's _______________________ ability to handle this task?
explanation: A noun phrase such as lack of experience can be used as the subject of affect: Will his lack of experience affect his ability?

fullSentence: 'Don't forget to write or message me,' said Beatriz as she left.
gapFill: 'Don’t _______________________,' said Beatriz as she left.
tags: C1, fixed phrase, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Keep/stay in touch means continue communicating with someone. Get in touch usually means contact someone.

fullSentence: No changes are planned for the event.
gapFill: This event will _______________________ to plan.
tags: C1, future, fixed phrase, phrasal verbs
explanation: Go ahead means happen or proceed as planned. According to plan means in the way that was originally arranged.

fullSentence: Leo no longer believes he’ll find a flat by June.
gapFill: He has given _______________________ a flat by June.
tags: C1, noun phrases, phrasal verbs, prepositions
explanation: Give up hope of + -ing means stop believing that something will happen: he has given up hope of finding a flat.

fullSentence: It’s hard to say what I’d have done in that scenario.
gapFill: I’m not _______________________ in that scenario.
answer: sure how I would have reacted
certain how I would have reacted
tags: C1, indirect questions, past modals, modals
explanation: After sure/certain, use an indirect question with how + subject + verb: I'm not sure how I would have reacted.

fullSentence: I don’t think the business will make a profit this year, considering the economy.
gapFill: Given the economic climate, _______________________ the business made a profit this year.
explanation: Would be surprised if + past simple can express that a present or future event seems unlikely: I would be surprised if the business made a profit.

fullSentence: This gate must remain open at all times.
answer: account should this gate be kept
tags: C1, modal verbs, inversion, passive voice
explanation: When a negative expression such as on no account comes first, use inversion: On no account should this gate be closed.

fullSentence: None of Anna’s suggestions were backed by the rest of the team.
gapFill: Anna’s suggestions met with _______________________ the rest of the team.
explanation: Meet with + noun can describe the reaction something receives: the suggestions met with no support from the team.

fullSentence: Alba is quickly gaining a reputation as a talented filmmaker.
gapFill: Alba is making _______________________ herself as a filmmaker.
explanation: Make a name for yourself means become well known or respected, especially in a particular field.

fullSentence: After this morning’s briefing, there will be a short feedback session.
gapFill: This morning’s briefing _______________________ a short feedback session.
explanation: Use be followed by to show that one event comes after another: the briefing will be followed by a feedback session.

fullSentence: I’d love to show you around when you come to Lisbon.
gapFill: It will be a _______________________ tour when you come to Lisbon.
answer: pleasure to take you on a
pleasure to take you for a
explanation: The fixed structure it is/will be a pleasure to + infinitive is a polite way of saying that you are happy to do something.

fullSentence: Omar volunteered with a local youth charity last summer.
gapFill: Omar _______________________ with a local youth charity last summer.
explanation: Work as + job/role describes the function someone performs: Omar worked as a volunteer.

fullSentence: Isla was just about to step out when she got the call.
gapFill: Isla was _______________________ out when she got the call.
explanation: Be on the point of + -ing means be just about to do something: Isla was on the point of stepping out.

fullSentence: I didn’t know that Nina had chosen to attend the workshop.
gapFill: I was unaware _______________________ attend the workshop.
explanation: Unaware is followed by of + noun phrase. Decision is followed by the to-infinitive: unaware of Nina's decision to attend.

fullSentence: When it comes to reliability, Luca is just like his father.
gapFill: As _______________________, Luca is just like his father.
explanation: As far as ... is concerned means when considering a particular subject: as far as reliability is concerned.

fullSentence: It took Jules ten minutes to find her sunglasses.
gapFill: Jules _______________________ for her sunglasses.
tags: C1, verb patterns, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Use spend + period of time + -ing to say how long an activity takes: she spent ten minutes looking for her sunglasses.

fullSentence: ‘Sorry, sir, is this your wallet?’ the attendant asked.
gapFill: ‘Excuse me, sir, but _______________________?’ the attendant asked.
answer: does this wallet belong to you
explanation: Belong is followed by to: belong to someone. It is not used with a direct object.

fullSentence: Please let us know if you change your booking.
gapFill: Please ensure that _______________________ change in your booking.
explanation: The formal pattern is notify someone of something: notify us of any change.

fullSentence: The roof repairs are planned for next Saturday.
gapFill: The roof repairs _______________________ place next Saturday.
tags: C1, fixed phrase, passive voice, prepositions
explanation: Be scheduled to + infinitive means be officially planned to happen: the repairs are scheduled to take place.

fullSentence: Layla struggled a lot to convince her manager to approve the leave.
gapFill: Layla had _______________________ her manager to approve the leave.
tags: C1, gerunds and infinitives, noun phrases
explanation: Use have difficulty (in) + -ing to describe something that is hard to do: she had great difficulty convincing her manager.

fullSentence: Americans continue to eat fast food even though it’s unhealthy.
gapFill: Americans still eat fast food despite _______________________ unhealthy.
explanation: Despite can be followed by the fact (that) + clause: despite the fact that it is unhealthy.

fullSentence: The tomatoes would have ripened earlier if the weather had been sunnier.
gapFill: The tomatoes would have ripened earlier _______________________ more sunshine.
explanation: In a third conditional, use if + past perfect for the unreal past condition: if there had been more sunshine.

fullSentence: They say the new restaurant is excellent.
gapFill: The new restaurant _______________________ excellent.
explanation: Passive reporting structures use be + past participle + to-infinitive: the restaurant is said to be excellent.

fullSentence: I’ve worked here for a few months and I’m only just beginning to feel comfortable.
gapFill: It’s taken me a few months _______________________ in this company.
explanation: Get used to means gradually become accustomed to something. Here to is a preposition, so it is followed by a noun or -ing form: get used to working.

fullSentence: Ali said he would not apologise and stormed out of the room.
gapFill: Ali _______________________ sorry and stormed out of the room.
tags: B2, reporting verbs, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Refuse is followed by the to-infinitive: refuse to do something. It means say firmly that you will not do it.

fullSentence: In my view, wearing jeans to a wedding is inappropriate.
gapFill: In my view, _______________________ to a wedding wearing jeans.
explanation: Ought to is a modal-like expression used for advice or judgement. The negative form is ought not to + infinitive.

fullSentence: Emily found a bracelet in her bag but had no idea who it belonged to.
gapFill: Emily found a bracelet in her bag but had no _______________________ be.
tags: B2, relative clauses, indirect questions, questions
explanation: In an indirect question, use statement word order: whose it might be, not whose might it be. Whose can stand alone when the noun is understood.

fullSentence: All the chairs were broken except that wooden one.
gapFill: That wooden chair was the _______________________ broken.
explanation: The structure the only one + to-infinitive identifies the single exception: the only one not to be broken.

fullSentence: Lara felt hurt because nobody had invited her to the picnic.
gapFill: Lara felt hurt because she _______________________ to the picnic.
explanation: Use the past perfect passive had been + past participle for a passive action that happened before another past event: she had not been invited.

fullSentence: Social workers don't earn nearly as much as doctors.
gapFill: Doctors _______________________ social workers.
explanation: Far can intensify a comparative: far more than means much more than.

fullSentence: Tania doesn’t want to go to the cinema tonight.
gapFill: Tania _______________________ going to the cinema tonight.
tags: B2, phrasal verbs, verb patterns, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Feel like + -ing means want to do something: she doesn't feel like going to the cinema.

fullSentence: I didn’t expect the book to be so moving.
gapFill: The book _______________________ really moving.
tags: B2, phrasal verbs, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Turn out to be means eventually prove to be or be discovered to be something: the book turned out to be very moving.

fullSentence: They completed the hike even though it rained all day.
gapFill: Despite the _______________________ completing the hike.
explanation: Succeed is followed by in + -ing: succeed in completing something. Despite is followed by a noun or -ing form.

fullSentence: Our hotel menu includes more than forty different dishes.
gapFill: There _______________________ over forty different dishes on our menu.
explanation: A choice of + plural noun means a range of different options: a choice of over forty dishes.

fullSentence: 'We don't believe that more roads will solve traffic problems,' said the engineers.
gapFill: The engineers announced that they _______________________ solve traffic problems.
explanation: Doubt can be followed by that, whether or if + clause. In reported speech after a past reporting verb, will commonly backshifts to would.

fullSentence: 'I'm definitely not leaving the country this year,' said Mr Riley.
gapFill: 'I have _______________________ the country this year,' said Mr Riley.
tags: B2, fixed phrase, noun phrases, formal
explanation: Use have no intention of + -ing to express a firm decision not to do something: no intention of leaving.

fullSentence: 'Maybe I was wrong about the time of the interview,' said Zoe.
gapFill: 'I may _______________________ about the time of the interview,' said Zoe.
tags: B2, modal verbs, deduction, past modals
explanation: Use may have + past participle for a possible past action: I may have made a mistake.

fullSentence: It’s too late now to go to the party.
gapFill: There is _______________________ to the party now.
tags: B2, fixed phrase, noun phrases, prepositions
explanation: There is no/little point in + -ing means that doing something is useless or not worthwhile.

fullSentence: Sam said, 'You can borrow my camera, if you agree to look after it.'
gapFill: Sam said I could borrow his camera _______________________ to look after it.
explanation: As long as and so long as introduce a condition and mean provided that: as long as I agreed to look after it.

fullSentence: The popularity of yoga has grown over the past ten years.
gapFill: Yoga _______________________ now than ten years ago.
explanation: Much can intensify a comparative adjective: much more popular means considerably more popular.

fullSentence: My uncle has decided not to smoke anymore, which is a smart choice.
gapFill: My uncle's decision _______________________ is a smart one.
tags: B2, verb patterns, gerunds and infinitives, phrasal verbs
explanation: Give up + -ing means stop doing an activity or habit: give up smoking. Decision is followed by the to-infinitive: the decision to give up.

fullSentence: My students completed very few writing assignments this term.
gapFill: Hardly _______________________ by my students this term.
explanation: Hardly any + plural countable noun means very few: hardly any writing assignments were completed.

fullSentence: I ignored how Ben was acting during the meeting.
gapFill: I didn’t pay _______________________ Ben was acting.
explanation: The expression is pay attention to + noun or clause: pay attention to how someone is acting. In a negative sentence, any is common: didn't pay any attention.

fullSentence: Sophie still finds it odd to write emails in English at work.
gapFill: Sophie still has not _______________________ emails in English at work.
tags: B2, verb patterns, used to, prepositions
explanation: Get used to + noun/-ing means become accustomed to something. Here to is a preposition, so use writing rather than write.

fullSentence: ‘Can my son try this jumper on?’ asked Maria.
gapFill: Maria asked the assistant _______________________ on that jumper.
tags: B2, indirect questions, reported speech, questions
explanation: Reported yes/no questions use if or whether + subject + verb, with statement word order: she asked if her son could try it on.

fullSentence: ‘Don't sit too close to the TV screen for a long time,’ the optician told us.
gapFill: The optician _______________________________________ too close to the TV screen for a long time.
tags: B2, reported speech, reporting verbs, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Warn someone not to + infinitive is used to advise someone against doing something because it may be dangerous or harmful.

fullSentence: We got lost trying to get back from the museum.
explanation: Find your way back means manage to return to a place, especially when navigation is involved: we couldn't find our way back.

fullSentence: Tom passed his final exam easily.
tags: B2, fixed phrase, noun phrases, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Use have no/little difficulty (in) + -ing to say that something is easy or causes few problems: he had no difficulty passing the exam.

fullSentence: I always rely on David’s advice.
explanation: Whose is a possessive relative pronoun and is followed by a noun: David is somebody whose advice I rely on.

fullSentence: We appear to have gone to the wrong train platform.
gapFill: It _______________________________________ we've gone to the wrong train platform.
explanation: Seem, appear and look can be followed by as if/as though + clause to describe how a situation appears: it seems as if we've gone to the wrong platform.

fullSentence: I didn’t understand the explanation for the maths problem.
gapFill: The explanation for the maths problem didn’t _______________________________________ me.
explanation: Make sense to someone means be understandable or logical to them: the explanation didn't make any sense to me.

fullSentence: It's a shame we didn’t travel more when we lived abroad.
gapFill: I wish that we _______________________________________ more when we lived abroad.
tags: B2, unreal forms, modal verbs, past modals
explanation: Use wish + could have + past participle to express regret about a missed possibility or opportunity in the past: I wish we could have travelled more.

fullSentence: She described the apartment to us in detail.
explanation: The noun form of describe is description. Use give someone a description of something: she gave us a detailed description of the apartment.

fullSentence: The instructions were so tricky that none of the students could follow them.
gapFill: The instructions were _______________________________________ the students to follow.
explanation: Use too + adjective + for someone + to-infinitive when something is excessively difficult, large, etc. for a person to do: too complicated for the students to follow.

fullSentence: Sandra broke the window by mistake.
tags: B2, verb patterns, past simple, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Mean to + infinitive means intend to do something. In the negative, didn't mean to shows that an action was accidental.

fullSentence: Lena has already planned her next trip to Italy.
gapFill: Lena has already _______________________________________ her next trip to Italy.
tags: B2, fixed phrase, noun phrases, prepositions
explanation: Make arrangements for + noun means organise or plan something in advance: make arrangements for a trip.

fullSentence: They say the forests in this region are disappearing.
gapFill: The forests in this region _______________________________________ disappearing.
explanation: Passive reporting structures use be + past participle + to-infinitive: the forests are said to be disappearing.

fullSentence: We didn’t enjoy our meal outside because it started to rain.
tags: B2, gerunds and infinitives, verb patterns, prepositions
explanation: Use prevent + person + from + -ing: the rain prevented us from enjoying our meal.

fullSentence: It looks like Luca has left his wallet at home.
explanation: After seem, use the perfect infinitive to have + past participle to refer to an earlier action: Luca seems to have left his wallet at home.

fullSentence: A trainee dentist took out Mr Silva’s tooth.
explanation: Use have + object + past participle when someone else performs a service or action for you: Mr Silva had his tooth taken out.

fullSentence: Ben only failed the test because he overslept.
explanation: A third conditional uses if + past perfect and would have + past participle for an unreal past result: if he had not overslept, he would have passed.

fullSentence: The manager postponed the excursion until after the inspection.
gapFill: The excursion _______________________________________ until after the inspection.
answer: was put off by the manager
explanation: Put off means postpone. In the passive, use be + put off: the excursion was put off.

fullSentence: ‘Can you tell me how wide this sofa is?’ Liam asked his dad.
explanation: Indirect questions use statement word order: how wide the sofa was, not how wide was the sofa.

fullSentence: Ella spent ages sorting out her files.
explanation: Use it takes + person + period of time + to-infinitive to say how long an activity requires: it took Ella ages to sort out her files.

fullSentence: An architect designed the building for Professor Klein.
gapFill: Professor Klein _______________________________________ by an architect.
tags: B2, causative have, passive voice, causative
explanation: The causative structure have + object + past participle shows that someone arranges for another person to do something: she had the building designed.

fullSentence: 'Luca, you broke the window!' shouted his neighbour.
tags: B2, reporting verbs, gerunds and infinitives, reported speech
explanation: Accuse is followed by person + of + -ing: accuse someone of breaking something. Having + past participle can emphasise that the action happened earlier.

fullSentence: Freya fell down the stairs because she wasn’t watching where she was going.
gapFill: If Freya  _______________________________________ to where she was going, she wouldn’t have fallen.
explanation: For an unreal past condition, use if + past perfect. The continuous form can describe an ongoing activity: if she had been paying attention.

fullSentence: It might not be easy for us to find accommodation at short notice.
gapFill: It _______________________________________ us to find accommodation at short notice.
explanation: Could can express possibility. The pattern could be + adjective + for someone + to-infinitive describes something that may be difficult: it could be hard for us to find accommodation.

fullSentence: You should have asked me before borrowing my shoes.
gapFill: You _______________________________________ me before borrowing my shoes.
explanation: Ought to have + past participle, like should have, is used to criticise or regret a past action: you ought to have asked.

fullSentence: Several flights were cancelled as a result of the heavy fog.
gapFill: Several flights were cancelled _______________________________________ so heavy.
explanation: Because is followed by a clause with a subject and verb, while because of is followed by a noun phrase: because the fog was heavy / because of the heavy fog.

fullSentence: I last got a message from Clara six months ago.
explanation: Use the present perfect negative with for + period to describe how long something has not happened: I haven't heard from Clara for six months.

fullSentence: I don’t recommend booking tickets through that website.
gapFill: It’s _______________________________________ tickets through that website.
explanation: Advisable is followed by the to-infinitive: it is advisable to book. Not advisable means something is not recommended.

fullSentence: Lara’s aunt founded the travel agency in 1988.
explanation: Set up is a phrasal verb meaning establish or start an organisation or business. In the passive: the agency was set up by her aunt.

fullSentence: The number of people working from home has gone up in the last two years.
gapFill: There _______________________________________ in the number of people working from home in the last two years.
explanation: A trend can be expressed with there has been + noun of change + in: there has been a rise in the number of people.

fullSentence: Jacob said he would never mention the incident again.
tags: B2, reported speech, gerunds and infinitives, verb patterns
explanation: Discuss is a transitive verb, so it takes a direct object without about: discuss the incident, not discuss about the incident.

fullSentence: 'This is the nicest Airbnb I've ever stayed in,' said Jordan.
tags: B2, comparatives and superlatives, present perfect
explanation: A superlative idea can be expressed with never + present perfect + comparative: I've never stayed in a nicer Airbnb.

fullSentence: There were very few people at the poetry reading on Monday.
gapFill: Hardly _______________________________________ the poetry reading on Monday.
explanation: Hardly anyone/anybody means almost nobody. Although the meaning is negative, the verb itself is affirmative: hardly anyone came.

fullSentence: We had to complete the report before we could leave the office.
gapFill: We had to stay in the office ____________________________ the report.
explanation: Until introduces the point when a situation ends. For two past events, either the past simple or past perfect may be possible depending on the emphasis.

fullSentence: Ella hadn’t expected the exhibition to be so good.
gapFill: The exhibition ____________________________ Ella had expected.
explanation: Use a comparative + than to compare reality with an expectation: the exhibition was better than Ella had expected.

fullSentence: If Josh doesn’t study more, he won’t pass the final exam.
gapFill: Josh won’t pass the final exam ____________________________ studying.
explanation: Unless means if ... not: he won't pass unless he studies more. Do more studying is another way of saying study more.

fullSentence: “Do you know what the problem is, Alex?” asked Priya.
tags: B2, indirect questions, reported speech, questions
explanation: Reported wh-questions use question word + subject + verb, without inversion: what the problem was.

fullSentence: The school decided to advertise the vacancy online.
gapFill: The school decided to ____________________________ the vacancy online.
explanation: Put an advertisement/ad/advert for something means publish an advertisement for it: put an advert for the vacancy online.

fullSentence: At the end of her presentation, the student congratulated her teacher.
gapFill: The student ____________________________ her teacher.
tags: B2, gerunds and infinitives, verb patterns
explanation: Use finish + noun + by + -ing to describe the action used to end something: she finished her presentation by congratulating her teacher.

fullSentence: I sent off my university application a month ago.
gapFill: It ____________________________ I sent off my university application.
explanation: Use it is/has been + period of time + since + past simple to say how much time has passed since an event.

fullSentence: The band received loads of fan mail after they had appeared on TV.
gapFill: The band received loads of fan mail ____________________________ on TV.
explanation: Following + noun is a more formal way of saying after: following their appearance on TV.

fullSentence: Mia is interested in learning more about photography.
gapFill: Mia would ____________________________ more about photography.
tags: B2, verb patterns, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Would like is followed by the to-infinitive: she would like to learn more.

fullSentence: Because of the roadworks, the police didn’t allow us to drive through the tunnel.
gapFill: The police wouldn’t ____________________________ through the tunnel.
tags: B2, causative, modal verbs, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Let is followed by object + bare infinitive, without to: let us drive, not let us to drive.

fullSentence: “Did you see the football match on Sunday?” asked Marco.
gapFill: Marco wanted to know if I had ____________________________ on Sunday.
explanation: Reported yes/no questions use if or whether + statement word order. The past perfect can show that the action happened before the reporting verb: if I had seen the match.

fullSentence: “I think this shirt is torn,” said Anna to the cashier.
gapFill: “I think ____________________________ this shirt,” Anna said to the cashier.
explanation: Torn is an adjective/past participle; the corresponding countable noun is tear: there is a tear in the shirt.

fullSentence: Leo always ignores everything I suggest.
gapFill: Leo never pays ____________________________ I suggest.
explanation: The expression is pay attention to + noun or clause: pay attention to what someone says or suggests.

fullSentence: “Could I borrow your tablet, Jason?” asked Emma.
gapFill: Emma asked Jason ____________________________ his tablet.
tags: B2, reporting verbs, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Lend means give something temporarily to another person, while borrow means receive it temporarily. Use lend + person + object: lend her his tablet.

fullSentence: Maybe Tom didn’t remember that we moved the deadline.
gapFill: Tom ____________________________ that we moved the deadline.
explanation: Use might have + past participle to express an uncertain possibility about the past: Tom might have forgotten.

fullSentence: All the students have a great time during the science workshop.
gapFill: Every ____________________________ during the science workshop.
answer: student has a lot of fun
explanation: Every is followed by a singular countable noun and a singular verb: every student has fun.

fullSentence: While I was in Berlin, I had some unforgettable experiences.
gapFill: During ____________________________ had some unforgettable experiences.
explanation: During is followed by a noun phrase, while while is normally followed by a clause: during my time in Berlin / while I was in Berlin.

fullSentence: You were careless to go out without switching the oven off.
gapFill: You ____________________________ the oven off before you went out.
explanation: Ought to have + past participle is used to say that a different action would have been better in the past: you ought to have switched the oven off.

fullSentence: “Is there any possibility that James will leave his partner?” asked Zoe.
gapFill: Zoe asked if there was any ____________________________ leaving his partner.
explanation: Chance of is followed by a noun or -ing form: a chance of James leaving. A possessive form before the gerund is also possible: a chance of James's leaving.

fullSentence: Sophie is the only one who responded to the email.
gapFill: Apart ____________________________ responded to the email.
explanation: Apart from + noun means except for. It can be followed by a negative expression such as nobody: apart from Sophie, nobody responded.

fullSentence: Do you feel comfortable with the new software yet?
gapFill: Have you ____________________________ the new software yet?
tags: B2, used to, verb patterns, perfect
explanation: Get used to + noun means become accustomed to something: have you got used to the new software yet?

fullSentence: It was such a cold day that nobody wanted to go outside.
gapFill: Nobody ____________________________ outside because it was so cold.
tags: B2, Gerunds and infinitives, phrasal verbs
explanation: Feel like + -ing means want to do something: nobody felt like going outside.

fullSentence: Daniel couldn’t speak or understand French.
gapFill: Besides ____________________________ French, Daniel couldn’t understand it either.
explanation: Besides is followed by a noun or -ing form. Unable is followed by the to-infinitive: besides being unable to speak French.

fullSentence: The meeting will begin immediately upon the CEO’s entrance.
gapFill: The meeting will begin ____________________________ the CEO enters.
explanation: As soon as introduces an action that happens immediately after another: the meeting will begin as soon as the CEO enters.

fullSentence: That’s the weirdest book I’ve ever read!
explanation: Such + a/an + adjective + singular noun can express strong emphasis: I've never read such a strange book.

fullSentence: A cheerful guide took us around the city.
tags: B2, Passive voice, verb forms, phrasal verbs
explanation: The passive is formed with be + past participle. Phrasal/prepositional elements stay with the verb: we were taken around the city.

fullSentence: My dad was determined to pay the bill.
tags: B2, reporting verbs, gerunds and infinitives, reported speech, prepositions
explanation: Insist on is followed by a noun or -ing form: he insisted on paying the bill.

fullSentence: The coach didn’t manage to convince Mia to join the team.
gapFill: The coach didn’t ____________________________ Mia to join the team.
tags: B2, verb patterns, prepositions, gerunds and infinitives, formal
explanation: Succeed is followed by in + -ing: succeed in convincing someone. It expresses successfully achieving something difficult.

fullSentence: “I’d prefer it if you didn’t eat in this room,” said the teacher.
gapFill: “Would you ____________________________ in this room?” said the teacher.
tags: B2, Gerunds and infinitives, verb patterns
explanation: Would you mind + -ing is used to make a polite request. For a negative request, use mind not + -ing: Would you mind not eating here?

fullSentence: Rachel impressed her interviewer by answering confidently.
gapFill: Rachel ____________________________ her interviewer by answering confidently.
explanation: The collocation is make a good impression on someone: Rachel made a good impression on her interviewer.

fullSentence: Hannah regrets not telling her friend the truth.
gapFill: Hannah ____________________________ her friend the truth.
tags: B2, unreal forms, past perfect, perfect
explanation: Use wish + past perfect to express regret about a past action: she wishes she had told her friend the truth.

fullSentence: I struggled to understand the safety guidelines.
gapFill: I ____________________________ the safety guidelines.
tags: B2, Gerunds and infinitives, fixed phrase, noun phrases
explanation: Have trouble + -ing means experience difficulty doing something: I had trouble understanding the guidelines.

fullSentence: Lara was so nervous she had difficulty following the examiner’s instructions.
gapFill: Lara was so nervous she ____________________________ the examiner’s instructions.
explanation: Use find it + adjective + to-infinitive to describe how easy or difficult an action is: she found it hard to follow the instructions.

fullSentence: They have postponed the concert and it will now happen next month.
gapFill: The concert ____________________________ until next month.
tags: B2, phrasal verbs, passive voice, verbs forms
explanation: Put off means postpone. In the present perfect passive, use has/have been put off.

fullSentence: I don’t plan on playing with Marcus again.
gapFill: I’ve got ____________________________ with Marcus again.
explanation: The pattern is have/got no intention of + -ing: I've got no intention of playing with Marcus again.

fullSentence: It seems a short circuit caused the explosion.
gapFill: The explosion ____________________________ by a short circuit.
explanation: Use seem + perfect passive infinitive, to have been + past participle, when a past event appears to have happened to the subject: the explosion seems to have been caused by a short circuit.

fullSentence: The town was dead in winter, so it wasn’t worth going out.
gapFill: The town was dead in winter, so ____________________________ going out.
tags: B2, fixed phrase, verb patterns, noun phrases
explanation: There is no/little point (in) + -ing means that doing something is useless or not worthwhile.

fullSentence: I called the doctor, but they told me I didn’t need an appointment.
gapFill: I called the doctor, but they said I ____________________________ an appointment.
tags: B2, modal verbs, obligation, reported speech
explanation: Didn't have to + infinitive means something was not necessary. It does not mean that the action was prohibited.

fullSentence: “I’ll take you to the airport if you’re packed,” said Jake.
gapFill: Jake said he’d take me to the airport ____________________________ packed.
explanation: As long as and so long as mean provided that and introduce a condition: as long as I was packed.

fullSentence: My phone needs to be fixed again.
explanation: Get + object + past participle is a causative structure used when someone else does something for you: get my phone fixed.

fullSentence: Sales decreased because of the pandemic, the company said.
gapFill: The company blamed the ____________________________ the pandemic.
tags: B2, noun phrase, prepositions, reporting verbs, reported speech
explanation: Blame something on someone/something means say that it caused a problem: the company blamed the fall in sales on the pandemic.

fullSentence: Ellie regretted wasting so much time online.
gapFill: Ellie ____________________________ so much time online.
tags: B2, wish, past perfect, verb forms, unreal forms
explanation: Use wish + past perfect for regret about the past: Ellie wished she had not wasted so much time.

fullSentence: People think the song was about his childhood.
gapFill: That song ____________________________ written about his childhood.
tags: B2, passive voice, reported speech, perfect
explanation: In a passive reporting structure referring to an earlier passive action, use be thought + to have been + past participle: the song is thought to have been written about his childhood.

fullSentence: I couldn’t have passed the exam if you hadn’t helped.
gapFill: I wouldn’t have passed the exam if ____________________________ your help.
tags: B2, unreal conditional, fixed expression (if it hadn’t been for)
explanation: If it had not been for + noun means without that person or thing: if it hadn't been for your help.

fullSentence: The platoon left almost no soldiers behind.
explanation: Hardly any + plural noun means almost none. In the passive: hardly any soldiers were left behind.

fullSentence: “What’s the height of that mountain?” She asked.
tags: B2, indirect questions, questions, reported speech
explanation: To ask about a measurement, use how + adjective: how high, how wide, how long, etc. Indirect questions use statement word order: how high the mountain was.

fullSentence: This sofa is almost the same as the one we saw yesterday.
gapFill: There isn’t ____________________________ this sofa and the one we saw yesterday.
tags: B2, comparatives and superlatives, noun phrases
explanation: Not much difference between two things means that they are very similar: there isn't much difference between them.

fullSentence: Maria wouldn’t apologise for shouting at us.
gapFill: Maria refused to ____________________________ shouting at us.
tags: B2, reporting verbs, verb forms, prepositions, reported speech
explanation: Say you are sorry for + -ing means apologise for an action: say she was sorry for shouting.

fullSentence: This town’s restaurants are what visitors enjoy the most.
gapFill: What most visitors ____________________________ this town is its restaurants.
tags: B2, verb patterns, fixed phrase, cleft sentences, comparatives and superlatives
explanation: Find + object + adjective means consider or experience something in a particular way: visitors find the restaurants enjoyable.

fullSentence: Our team probably won’t manage to get the grant.
gapFill: Our team is unlikely to ____________________________ the grant.
tags: B2, verb patterns, gerunds and infinitives, probability, speculation
explanation: Succeed is followed by in + -ing: succeed in getting the grant. Be unlikely to expresses low probability.

fullSentence: We last spoke on the phone two years ago.
gapFill: It’s ____________________________ we last spoke on the phone.
tags: B2, time expressions, present perfect, verb forms
explanation: Use it has been + period of time + since + past simple to say how long ago something happened: it's been two years since we last spoke.

fullSentence: “You weren’t honest with me,” Anna told Paul.
tags: B2, reporting verbs, verb patterns, reported speech, prepositions
explanation: Accuse is followed by person + of + -ing: accuse someone of not being honest.

fullSentence: You really ought to get to the interview on time.
gapFill: I strongly advise you ____________________________ for the interview.
tags: B2, reporting verbs, verb forms, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Advise is followed by object + to-infinitive. For negative advice, use advise someone not to + infinitive.

fullSentence: We managed to win the race, even though we weren’t well prepared.
gapFill: We won the race ____________________________ badly prepared.
explanation: In spite of is followed by a noun or -ing form: in spite of being badly prepared. Having been can emphasise that the state existed before the main event.

fullSentence: The journey to Barcelona lasts two hours by plane.
tags: B2, verb forms, time expressions, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Use it takes + period of time + to-infinitive to express the duration of an activity: it takes two hours to fly to Barcelona.

fullSentence: I didn’t know the hotel was that far from the station.
gapFill: I didn’t know the hotel ____________________________ way from the station.
explanation: Such + a/an + adjective + noun can emphasise degree: such a long way from the station.

fullSentence: Dan missed the bus because he didn’t leave on time.
gapFill: If Dan had left on time, he would ____________________________ bus.
tags: B2, conditionals, past modals, modal verbs
explanation: A third conditional uses if + past perfect and would have + past participle for an unreal past result: he would not have missed the bus.

fullSentence: This app performs considerably better than all the others.
gapFill: The other apps don’t work ____________________________ this one.
tags: B2, comparatives and superlatives, emphasis, intensifiers
explanation: Not nearly as + adverb/adjective + as means considerably less: the other apps don't work nearly as well as this one.

fullSentence: “Could I use your laptop for a second?” Mia asked Ben.
gapFill: Mia asked Ben ____________________________ his laptop for a second.
tags: B2, reported speech, questions, indirect questions, modal verbs
explanation: Reported yes/no questions can use whether + subject + verb, with statement word order: she asked whether she could use his laptop.

fullSentence: Lucas shows so much talent as a photographer—his pictures look unreal.
gapFill: Lucas is ____________________________ photographer that his pictures look unreal.
tags: B2, emphasis, noun phrases, intensifiers, so/such
explanation: Use such + a/an + adjective + singular noun + that to express a strong degree and its result: such a talented photographer that his pictures look unreal.

fullSentence: I wish I hadn’t drunk so much at the weekend.
tags: B2, advice, past modals, quantifiers, modal verbs, wish
explanation: Use should not have + past participle to express regret or criticism about a past action: I should not have drunk so much.

fullSentence: The train was delayed because a signal failed.
gapFill: The train’s delay ____________________________ signal failure.
tags: B2, causality, verb forms, passive voice
explanation: In the passive, cause is followed by by to introduce the cause: the delay was caused by a signal failure.

fullSentence: “Do you want to go to my presentation, Leo?” asked Mia.
tags: B2, reporting verbs, verb patterns, reported speech
explanation: Invite is followed by person + to + event/place: Mia invited Leo to her presentation.

fullSentence: Several drivers ignored the roadwork signs.
gapFill: Several drivers ____________________________ the roadwork signs.
tags: B2, fixed phrase, verb forms, noun phrases
explanation: Pay no attention to means ignore: several drivers paid no attention to the signs.

fullSentence: The volunteers had too little water for all the hikers.
gapFill: There ____________________________ the volunteers to give to all the hikers.
explanation: Enough comes before a noun: enough water. The pattern enough + noun + for someone + to-infinitive shows whether the quantity is sufficient for an action.

fullSentence: Eva gets no exercise other than cycling to school.
tags: B2, noun phrases, emphasis, cleft sentences
explanation: The only + noun + subject + verb can emphasise a single exception: the only exercise Eva gets is cycling to school.

fullSentence: Leo wanted to start painting so he quit his job as a coach.
tags: B2, phrasal verbs, verb patterns, gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Give up + noun/-ing means stop an activity. A following to-infinitive can express purpose: he gave up coaching to become a painter.

fullSentence: There’s far less pollution in Madrid than there once was.
gapFill: There isn’t ____________________________ Madrid as there used to be.
tags: B2, comparatives and superlatives, quantifiers, intensifiers
explanation: Not nearly as much + uncountable noun + as expresses a large difference in quantity: there isn't nearly as much pollution as there used to be.

fullSentence: In the documentary, witnesses describe their experiences vividly.
gapFill: The documentary ____________________________ the witnesses’ experiences.
explanation: Give an account of something means describe or report it. An adjective can describe the quality of the account: give a vivid account of the witnesses' experiences.

fullSentence: These delicate herbs are frequently damaged by mites and aphids.
gapFill: These herbs ____________________________ by mites and aphids.
explanation: Be prone to is followed by a noun or -ing form and means be likely to experience something, usually negative: these herbs are prone to being damaged.

fullSentence: Do you have any idea how Marta managed to fund such a lavish wedding?
gapFill: Can anyone ____________________________ Marta paid for such a lavish wedding?
tags: C2, fixed phrase, indirect questions, questions
explanation: Shed/cast/throw light on something means help to explain or clarify it: shed some light on how Marta paid for the wedding.

fullSentence: It took Oliver a while to accept that he wouldn’t be returning to the company.
gapFill: Oliver has finally ____________________________ he won't be going back to the company.
answer: come to terms with the fact that
Come to terms with the fact
explanation: Come to terms with + noun means gradually accept a difficult or unpleasant reality: come to terms with the fact that he won't be returning.

fullSentence: The attendees didn't expect Nina to start rapping during the presentation.
gapFill: It ____________________________ rapping during the presentation.
answer: took the attendees by surprise when Nina began
took the attendees aback when Nina began
took the attendees by surprise when Nina started
took the attendees aback when Nina started
tags: C2, fixed phrase, prepositions, phrasal verbs
explanation: Take someone by surprise or take someone aback means surprise them unexpectedly: Nina's sudden rapping took the attendees by surprise.

fullSentence: Leo bounced back from the flu in just a few days.
answer: not take Leo long to get over
not take long for Leo to get over
tags: C2, verb patterns, time expressions, phrasal verbs
explanation: Get over an illness means recover from it. The pattern it doesn't take someone long to + infinitive describes something happening quickly.

fullSentence: We had no idea how much destruction the fire had caused until it was out.
gapFill: It wasn’t until the fire was ____________________________ became apparent.
answer: extinguished that the extent of the destruction
put out that the extent of the destruction
out that the extent of the destruction
explanation: The cleft structure it wasn't until ... that emphasises when something finally became clear: it wasn't until the fire was out that the extent of the destruction became apparent.

fullSentence: As soon as she heard the news, Maya began to realise how fortunate she'd been.
